**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The Section 14 IP package already lands on our preferred position:

- **Customer Data / Customer IP (§ 14.1):** We own all Customer Data, Customer Confidential Information, Customer-provided material and independently developed IP; Vendor gets only a limited processing right to deliver the Services for us. § 15.1 reinforces this (no sale, no advertising use, no combination with other customers' data, no training a generally available model without our written consent).
- **Deliverables (§ 14.2):** Ownership vests in us on creation, backed by a present assignment from Vendor, equivalent assignments from its personnel, and a further-assurance covenant.
- **Licence-back (§ 14.3 → § 13.2):** Vendor keeps only Vendor Technology, and any Vendor Technology embedded in or required to use a Deliverable carries a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, fully paid licence to use, modify, create derivative works and permit contractor support for our business. Vendor must also flag material Vendor Technology pre-delivery and cannot bury restrictive third-party material in a Deliverable.
- **No joint ownership (§ 14.4):** Expressly excluded absent a signed instrument identifying exploitation rights; feedback is voluntary and we retain unrestricted rights in our own feedback.
- **Definitions check:** "Vendor Technology" (§ 1.8) carves out Customer Data and our pre-Effective Date IP, so there is no scope leakage back to Vendor.

One minor observation not worth a redline: § 1.4 limits "Deliverable" to work product an Order Form identifies as created specifically for us — ordinary scoping we can manage by drafting Order Form deliverable lists carefully.
